questions.prompt: What did Fern's plants do after Wren poured on the purple potion?
choices: All the plants began to walk.
All the plants grew bright fruit.
questions.answer: All the plants began to walk.
questions.evidenceText: Then all the plants began to walk.

questions.prompt: Why does Wren's potion make the plants walk?
choices: She follows a motion recipe from the wrong book.
She stirs the correct growing recipe too slowly.
She adds a seed that belongs in the Crystal Stream.
questions.answer: She follows a motion recipe from the wrong book.
questions.evidenceText:
She had used the wrong book.
"This is the motion recipe," she said.
"Not the growing recipe."

questions.prompt: What lesson does Fern's answer about fewer books teach Wren?
choices: Checking the right instructions matters more than having more books.
The purple colour meant the potion needed more stirring.
The walking plants showed the growing potion was too strong.
questions.answer: Checking the right instructions matters more than having more books.
questions.rationale: Wren's wrong book contains the motion recipe that made the plants walk, and Fern answers "Fewer books" when Wren asks for more; this shows checking the right instructions matters more than having more books.
questions.evidenceText:
"Yes," said Wren. "I need more books."
"Fewer," said Fern.
"Fewer books."
